subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Reference Price Manipulation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Reference Price Manipulation.

hook.text: A tag reads: was $200, now $99. You feel you saved $101. The item was never sold at $200. The reference was invented.

buildup.text: Reference prices set expectations. A sale discount feels valuable only compared to a higher original price, real.

discovery.text: Retailers inflate original prices before sales events. The discount is measured from a phantom price nobody ever paid.

twist.text: JCPenney tried honest pricing: no fake sales, fair prices. Sales dropped 25%. Customers missed the thrill of a deal.

climax.text: Ignoring the was-price changes your shopping. Ask: would I buy this at this price without a sale sign?

punchline.text: The sale price is the real price. The original was the lie.

quiz.question: What happened when JCPenney eliminated fake sales and offered honest pricing?
options: Sales increased because customers trusted the company
Sales dropped 25% because customers missed the thrill of deals
There was no change in customer behavior
